observations: Photo 0: close-up of a used V-type car engine, valve covers and timing belt/pulley assembly visible, no radiator or intake manifold attached.
A black plastic engine cover has a barcode sticker with partial text that may read 'V2G-A03' but is not clearly legible.
Watermark 'KINGSLEY MOTOR SPARE PARTS' overlays both photos.
Photo 1: wider shop view showing several stacked used engines and what looks like a transmission unit, with wooden/metal shelving marked 'NISSAN' in the background.
A person in a green shirt is partly visible, apparently handling wiring on one of the engines.
No manufacturer nameplate, engine code plate, or VIN-style tag is clearly readable on the engine itself in either photo.
No visual confirmation of the engine running, no compression test, no oil condition shown.

identity.kind: used car engine (possibly V6, type unclear)

claims.claim: We sell all kinds of quality japanese parts
claims.evidence: No readable manufacturer marking or country-of-origin stamp visible on the engine in either photo; 'NISSAN' text in background is on shelving, not on the item itself.
No start-up video, compression test, or oil/coolant condition shown.

risks.risk: Engine make/model cannot be confirmed, which drives price tier
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the engine ID plate, casting number, or ECU label
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced until model is identified

risks.risk: Engine may be non-functional or have internal wear/damage
risks.proof: Video of engine running or compression test results
Odometer photo from donor vehicle or import paperwork
risks.if_unproven: treated as unknown high-mileage used unit

risks.risk: Listing may show a different engine than the one actually sold (multiple units in stock photo)
risks.proof: Single clear photo of the exact unit for sale with a reference tag/number
risks.if_unproven: cannot confirm which unit corresponds to the offer

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code/ID plate or casting number
Photo or video showing the engine running or turning over
Clear single-item photo of the exact engine being sold, separate from the group shot
response.reason: The engine's brand and model cannot be read from either photo, which is required to find comparable listings and set even a worst-case price; a clear ID plate or model sticker photo is needed before pricing.
